- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is low or flat (0.00–0.18).  
- Underestimate sharp downward moves when sentiment is negative or neutral (0.00–0.27) — model tends to ignore downside risk.  
- Forecast mean reversion too aggressively after high sentiment peaks — model overcorrects downward.  
- When sentiment is consistently low (0.00), model tends to overpredict short-term recovery; adjust downward by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.  
- Avoid forecasting sharp upward moves when sentiment is weak — model often overreacts to minor price dips.  
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates volatility in early days after a spike — add 1–3% buffer to forecast if sentiment is >0.27.  
- If sentiment is >0.36, model tends to overforecast — reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–7 days.  
- When sentiment drops below 0.18, model often fails to recognize downward momentum — adjust forecast downward by 2–4% for next 3–5 days.
